component.name: Snag
component.summary: Download video and audio from almost any site

description.p: Snag is a small, fast desktop front end for yt-dlp. Paste a link, pick what you want, and it downloads: from YouTube and more than a thousand other sites.

ul.li: Video with sound, audio only, or video without sound
Pick the quality from what the site actually offers, and the file type for each download: mp4, webm, mkv or mov, or mp3, m4a, ogg, opus, flac or wav
Pick items out of a playlist, or take all of them
A queue with progress, speed and time left, that survives a restart
Clip a section of a video on a timeline, split by chapters, save subtitles
Remux, extract audio, mute or turn a file you already have into a GIF
A searchable history of everything downloaded
Presets for the downloads you keep making

description.p: Snag keeps yt-dlp up to date by itself, because sites change and an old yt-dlp is the usual reason a download stops working.

screenshot.caption: Paste a link and pick what you want
Settings for quality, codec, format and more

description.p: Background mode on Linux: a tray icon, closing to the tray, starting in the tray, and starting when you log in. Quit in the tray menu no longer turns background mode off for good.
A Windows fix: no duplicate Start menu entry for a machine-wide install.
The tray menu works on the first click, and closing to the tray no longer plays the minimise animation.
Fixes for the snap and the Flatpak: the snap's ffmpeg starts, its settings survive updates, and the Flatpak no longer loses a download saved to a folder the sandbox cannot see.

Linux packages: a .deb, an .rpm and a Flatpak alongside the AppImage, which now starts on current distributions without libfuse2. Converting a downloaded mkv to mp4 works, and "show in folder" selects the file.
Pick the format for each download, search history, and more formats: mov, m4a and flac. webm and wav downloads no longer fail at the very end.
Starting in the tray no longer flashes the window.
